system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Applied Machine Learning
Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example
PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than 4 years in data science
roles. Builds and evaluates forecasting and customer-propensity models, develops feature-engineered workflows in
Python and SQL, and translates business needs into practical analytical tools. Experience includes scheduled
model scoring and forecasting workflows using BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, a Dockerized Streamlit
experiment tool, and automated tests for forecasting feature code. Seeking to develop further in machine learning
engineering and production systems.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, pytest), SQL (BigQuery), dbt, Git, Docker,
Streamlit, R (tidyverse, brms), Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, Jupyter
Machine learning: Feature engineering, forecasting, churn propensity modelling, model evaluation, SHAP
Statistics: A/B testing, sequential testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics, time-series forecasting
EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions), Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
• Built a weekly, six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow by recipe and region using LightGBM and calendar,
price and menu-position features. The scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery
for operations reporting in Looker; WAPE fell from 23% to 14%, with estimated food waste reduction of 9%.
• Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery, with retention offers targeted to
top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validated a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group.
• Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests each year for growth and product teams; built a sequential
testing calculator used by around 25 colleagues, writing the Python Streamlit app and its Dockerfile. The data
platform team manages its Cloud Run deployment.
• Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
• Since 2025, have written pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.
• Present results to leadership monthly and delivered the internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
• Performed customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team about two days each month.
SELECTED PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal, 2025
• Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep learning course;
achieved approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project.
• Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.
EDUCATION
MSc Statistics, University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand
BSc Mathematics, University of the Lothians | 2019
LANGUAGES
English (native) | Swahili (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Quillstone AI Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. My experience
building and evaluating forecasting and customer-propensity models, developing Python and
SQL machine-learning workflows, including feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring, and
forecasting pipelines, and working closely with product and operations teams has given me a
practical foundation in applied machine learning workflows and production-oriented analytical
systems.
At Thistlebox, I built a weekly demand-forecasting workflow using LightGBM and engineered
calendar, price and menu-position features. It runs as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench
notebook and writes forecasts to BigQuery; forecast WAPE fell from 23% to 14%, with an
estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring
workflow in BigQuery, where a 10% holdout validated a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in
churn in the treated group. These projects have involved turning business needs into useful
models and data workflows, evaluating their impact, and communicating results to
stakeholders.
Alongside this work, I design and analyse around 40 A/B tests a year and built a Python
Streamlit sequential-testing tool used by about 25 colleagues. Since 2025, I have written
pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage; I also
wrote the Dockerfile for a Streamlit application used by around 25 colleagues. The data
platform team manages its Cloud Run deployment. I use BigQuery daily for production SQL
and batch churn scoring, maintain dbt models for the analytics layer, and have worked with
scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook jobs. I am keen to build further on this experience
in production machine learning engineering. My MSc in Statistics and BSc in Mathematics
support my work in modelling, experimentation and feature engineering.
Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants through its customer operations tools, and its
emphasis on team ownership, practical problem-solving and learning, make this role
particularly appealing to me. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience
in applied modelling, experimentation and analytical workflows could contribute to the AI
team through practical model evaluation, feature engineering, experimentation, and reliable
data workflows while developing further in production machine learning engineering.
Kind regards, Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
